chief_complaint: widespread muscle pain, chronic fatigue, poor sleep, and brain fog for 1 year
hpi_details: 38F reports 1 year of constant, widespread aching pain in muscles and joints all over her body. Accompanied by chronic exhaustion, waking up unrefreshed, and difficulty concentrating ('brain fog').
ideas: thinks she has chronic fatigue syndrome or fibromyalgia
concerns: worried she will never feel normal again

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Fibromyalgia is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes Evidence-based diagnostic and therapeutic protocol for Fibromyalgia (central sensitization pain syndrome), adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

Key HPI features: 38F reports 1 year of constant, widespread aching pain in muscles and joints all over her body. Accompanied by chronic exhaustion, waking up unrefreshed, and difficulty concentrating ('brain fog').
Objective/Exam findings: Complete vital signs and focused physical examination required. Diagnostic workup tailored for Fibromyalgia (central sensitization pain syndrome).
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Fibromyalgia.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Hypothyroidism without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Objective joint swelling or elevated inflammatory markers — would suggest a different diagnosis instead.
management_principles: Evidence-based diagnostic and therapeutic protocol for Fibromyalgia (central sensitization pain syndrome)
: Assess widespread pain and symptom severity using validated criteria; exclude alternative causes when clinically indicated (for example, CBC, ESR/CRP, and TSH)

Use education, pacing, graded aerobic/strength exercise, sleep support, and CBT when accessible; medication options such as duloxetine or low-dose amitriptyline require clinician-directed selection and monitoring for interactions, adverse effects, and pregnancy considerations.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: Patient presenting with symptoms of Fibromyalgia (central sensitization pain syndrome). widespread muscle pain, chronic fatigue, poor sleep, and brain fog for 1 year. 38F reports 1 year of constant, widespread aching pain in muscles and joints all over her body. Accompanied by chronic exhaustion, waking up unrefreshed, and difficulty concentrating ('brain fog').
reference_soap.objective: Complete vital signs and focused physical examination required. Diagnostic workup tailored for Fibromyalgia (central sensitization pain syndrome).
reference_soap.assessment: Clinical presentation highly suggestive of Fibromyalgia (central sensitization pain syndrome).
reference_soap.plan: Use validated widespread-pain/symptom-severity criteria and a focused examination; test for alternative conditions only when clinically indicated (for example CBC, ESR/CRP, and TSH). Explain that the pain is real and treat with education, pacing, sleep support, and graded activity; a clinician may consider medication after reviewing interactions, adverse effects, mental-health safety, and pregnancy considerations. Objective synovitis, persistent fever, focal neurologic deficit, unexplained weight loss, or abnormal inflammatory findings warrant reassessment rather than labeling the symptoms fibromyalgia.

teaching.one_liner: A central sensitization pain syndrome causing widespread muscle and joint pain, unrefreshing sleep, and cognitive fog, in the absence of inflammation or structural joint damage.
red_flags: Objective joint swelling or elevated inflammatory markers — would suggest a different diagnosis instead

must_ask.say: Is the pain all over your body, or in specific joints?
Do you wake up feeling rested, or still exhausted?
Have you had trouble concentrating, or 'brain fog'?
How long has this been going on?
Do you have irritable bowel syndrome or other chronic symptoms?
